overview: Two items on Japanese harbor development: a 1938 cross-reference to Grew's report on Takao's strategic significance (via Italian naval-attaché material), and a 1939 despatch on the new port at Gosei being named Niitaka, christened by Governor-General Kobayashi before officials and businessmen.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the Port of Takao and Japan’s “Southward Advance”
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to a report on the significance of the Port of Takao for Japan’s “Southward Advance” policy.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Grew's report assessing Takao's significance to Japan's 'Southward Advance,' enclosing a translated Italian naval-attaché report.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the naming of Niitaka Harbor
subfiles.from: John K. Emmerson, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Emmerson reports the official naming and christening of the new harbor at Gosei as Niitaka.
subfiles.summary: Emmerson reports the planned Gosei port was officially named Niitaka Ko, christened by Governor-General Kobayashi before 800-plus officials and businessmen.

interest: Shows Taiwan harbor development linking Takao's naval significance and the ceremonial naming of Niitaka port.
